unit: One existing feature title plus its complete explanation, classified as written. No activation examples, causal claims, or inferred generalization.
primary_question: Does the fraction of descriptions centered on semantic content or relations change with model depth?
secondary_question: Does the fraction centered on abstract concepts, relations or pragmatics change with depth?

categories.S: Surface form / formatting: character, literal string, subword fragment, punctuation, whitespace, capitalization, numeral spelling, code delimiters, chat markers, list markers or document formatting. The claim concerns recognizable form.
categories.G: Grammar / linguistic structure: parts of speech, syntactic positions or dependencies, tense, morphological role, grammatical constructions or phrase/clause boundaries. Meaning of a topic is not the defining criterion.
categories.C: Semantic content / topics: a class of entities, objects, actions, properties, sensory qualities or subject domains (animals, cities, software, medicine, physical movement). Topic breadth alone does not establish abstraction.
categories.A: Abstract / relational / pragmatic semantics: abstract concepts or mental states, beliefs, intent, uncertainty, norms, evaluation, causal/logical/comparative/quantity relations, discourse meaning or communicative intent. The claim concerns meaning or use, rather than merely a marker or grammatical construction.
categories.M: Mixed / unclear: inseparable cross-category conjunctions without a clear dominant target; vague or uninterpretable descriptions; explanations insufficient to choose. Never force a semantic or structural decision.

boundary_rules: Read the full explanation, not just the title. A word such as abstract, semantic, conceptual or detection in the title is not sufficient evidence.
Categorize the defining target. A positional condition around an otherwise clear semantic class need not make it mixed; unrelated coequal targets do.

A literal word or subword across arbitrary contexts is S. A grammatical role or construction is G. A meaning class with words as examples is C or A. Do not assume paraphrase invariance from wording alone.
Digits, numeral formatting and numbered-list markers are S. General quantity, numerical value, magnitude, counting or ordering meaning is A. A single number string alone is S.
Code punctuation, identifier fragments and keyword spelling are S; code grammatical constructions are G; computational meaning or purpose is C or A.
List/document formatting and chat role delimiters are S. Sentence grammatical organization is G. Discourse contrast, requests, refusal, uncertainty or narrative purpose described as meaning/use is A.
Nouns/adjectives as parts of speech are G. Nouns denoting a topic/object/property class are C. Abstract concepts/mental/normative/relational meaning is A.
Do not infer a category from assumed depth, transform rank, activity, evaluation scores or prior examples. These metadata are hidden.
This describes an annotation claim. Do not endorse the explanation as a validated feature function.

output.category: S, G, C, A or M
output.reason: At most 14 words describing the decisive target; no private reasoning transcript.

examples.text: Closing parentheses and commas in function calls
Final subword -tion or -ing irrespective of the surrounding topic
Passive verb constructions after auxiliary verbs
Abstract noun phrase in direct object position, regardless of topic
Names of birds and other flying animals
Doubt about whether a factual claim is correct
Comparison of amounts or causal dependence between events
Commas, kitchen tools and expressions of regret with no common account

sampling.eligibility: Nonempty title and explanation; uniformly sample without replacement within layer.
sampling.calibration: Two per layer, all three Luna annotators, excluded from main estimates.
sampling.main: Forty new per layer; shuffled round-robin primary assignments to three annotators so each sees every layer. Two random main items per layer independently coded by all three.
sampling.blinding: Only opaque ID, title and explanation are shown in randomized order. No layer, transform ID, rank, activity, quality scores or trend hypothesis.
sampling.go_rule: Proceed if pairwise coarse agreement (S/G vs C/A vs M) on calibration is at least 80%; otherwise revise boundaries and recalibrate before viewing layer trends.
sampling.consensus: For shared main items choose majority category; three-way disagreement becomes M. Retain all original labels. Main non-overlap items have a single primary rating.

analysis.denominator: All 40 randomly sampled explained features per layer, including M. Missing catalog explanations are reported separately.
analysis.uncertainty: Wilson 95% intervals describe sampling of descriptions conditional on the available explained catalog; they do not include systematic annotation or explanation error.
analysis.coarse_agreement: Pairwise raw agreement and Cohen kappa on S/G vs C/A vs M; fine agreement on five categories.
analysis.trend: Descriptive Spearman correlation on 36 layer fractions and 12-layer early/middle/late averages. No claim of monotonically increasing or causal abstraction.
analysis.robustness: Display explained/all slots, semantic fraction among non-M, M-as-semantic upper bound, ambiguity threshold sensitivity, and semantic lower/upper bounds if every missing explanation is nonsemantic/semantic.
prohibitions: Do not use a keyword classifier as a substitute for the requested independent model annotations.
Do not claim LLM agreement validates biology-like hierarchy or feature causality.
